description: A junior computer science student with a strong background in low-level development from a previous cybersecurity internship, seeking to deepen their understanding of kernel-level security.

nodes.description: Analyze the fundamental structures of operating systems, focusing on the distinction between kernel and user modes and the architecture of system calls.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Because the student has strong prior exposure, we proceed directly to core architectural concepts without introductory scaffolding.
nodes.title: OS Structures & Dual-Mode Operation

nodes.description: Explore the performance implications of system calls and context switching, including overhead analysis in high-performance environments.
nodes.title: Advanced Performance Analysis of Kernel Transitions
nodes.personalizationRationale: This enrichment node leverages the student's strong prior exposure to systems programming to analyze low-level architectural performance costs.

nodes.description: Master the process abstraction, including lifecycle states, process control blocks, and the mechanics of context switching.
nodes.title: Process Lifecycle & Management
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core process management theory is required for all students to ensure success on exam-tested material.

nodes.description: Deep dive into IPC implementation details, comparing the throughput and latency of shared memory versus message-passing in modern kernels.
nodes.title: High-Performance Inter-Process Communication
nodes.personalizationRationale: Given the student's strong prior exposure, this node explores the trade-offs of IPC mechanisms used in high-concurrency systems.

nodes.description: Examine threading models and the implementation of threading libraries (Pthreads) for concurrent application development.
nodes.title: Threading Models & Libraries
nodes.personalizationRationale: Thread management is a core requirement; student's strong prior exposure allows for a faster pace through standard library usage.

nodes.description: Evaluate CPU scheduling criteria and algorithms, such as Round Robin, Priority, and Multi-Level Feedback Queues.
nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Algorithms & Evaluation
nodes.personalizationRationale: As scheduling is heavily tested on the midterm, this core node ensures theoretical mastery of all required algorithms.

nodes.description: A comprehensive review and assessment of Chapters 1-5 material to prepare for the week-8 midterm exam.
nodes.personalizationRationale: This required assessment node ensures the student's strong prior exposure translates into mastery of course-specific exam criteria.
nodes.title: Midterm Assessment: OS Basics & Scheduling

nodes.description: Implement synchronization primitives including mutexes, semaphores, and monitors to solve the critical section problem.
nodes.title: Synchronization Primitives & Mutexes
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core synchronization concepts are essential for the required programming projects and final exam.

nodes.description: Analyze lock-free synchronization techniques and atomic operations as alternatives to traditional locking mechanisms in modern systems.
nodes.personalizationRationale: The student's strong prior exposure allows for enrichment into lock-free programming, a more complex synchronization paradigm.
nodes.title: Advanced Concurrency: Lock-Free Programming

nodes.description: Model deadlock characterization and apply avoidance strategies like the Banker's Algorithm to systems problems.
nodes.title: Deadlock Prevention & Avoidance
nodes.personalizationRationale: Despite the student's strong prior exposure, deadlock characterization is a mandatory theoretical component of the course.

nodes.description: Study memory addressing, contiguous allocation, and the transition to paging and segmentation.
nodes.title: Main Memory & Paging Structures
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required for the memory management project; covers foundational physical memory concepts.

nodes.description: Analyze demand paging and virtual memory performance, including advanced page replacement policies and thrashing analysis.
nodes.title: Virtual Memory Performance & Policies
nodes.personalizationRationale: Enrichment node focusing on performance modeling of virtual memory, appropriate for students with strong prior systems exposure.

nodes.description: Examine I/O subsystems, device drivers, and the implementation of file systems including inodes and directory structures.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Essential capstone material covering the final pillars of operating systems required for the final exam.
nodes.title: I/O Subsystems & File Storage Structure

nodes.description: Compare modern file system designs, such as Log-Structured File Systems (LFS) and Journaling, for reliability and performance.
nodes.title: Advanced File System Design & Reliability
nodes.personalizationRationale: Leverages the student's strong prior exposure to explore modern storage optimizations and consistency models.

nodes.title: Final Cumulative Review & Synthesis
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory final review assessment to ensure readiness for the cumulative final exam, tailored with advanced synthesis questions for this student's strong prior exposure.
nodes.description: Final review of the cumulative syllabus, including all blocks from foundations through file systems.
